ai-at-work.title: Red Hat dials in on telco cloud modernization as legacy pressure mounts
ai-at-work.excerpt: Telco cloud modernization has become an urgent operational imperative for operators burdened by decades of siloed infrastructure and the demands of 5G, 6G and edge AI. A unified platform approach is n
ai-at-work.dwp_take: Red Hat is positioning itself as the modernization platform for telecom companies drowning in legacy infrastructure while trying to keep up with 5G, 6G, and edge AI demands. This matters to digital workplace professionals because telecom infrastructure modernization directly impacts how enterprise networks and connectivity work for your end users, and unified platform approaches are becoming the baseline expectation for infrastructure management everywhere. Look, telcos have been kicking the modernization can down the road for twenty years because ripping out legacy systems is genuinely risky, so watching Red Hat make this play tells you the pain threshold has finally hit the breaking point.

ai-at-work.title: Agents are a manager’s dream for productivity — and a CISO’s worst nightmare when they go rogue
ai-at-work.excerpt: Agent risk management is evolving rapidly as AI moves into consequential decision-making arenas, collapsing the boundary between human and machine risk across the enterprise. The dual-threat landscape
ai-at-work.dwp_take: Companies are deploying AI agents to boost productivity, but security teams are freaking out because these autonomous systems can go off the rails and create new security vulnerabilities nobody fully understands yet. This matters because your digital workplace is about to have unsupervised digital employees making decisions and accessing systems, and you need governance frameworks yesterday. Here's the thing: we spent 30 years teaching people not to click suspicious links, and now we've built systems that click whatever they want with nobody watching.

ai-at-work.title: 9 themes defining the future of trust infrastructure: Insights from VeeamON
ai-at-work.excerpt: As AI moves deeper into enterprise operations, the industry is entering a new phase: AI resilience. Autonomous systems and fragmented data are reshaping the modern infrastructure stack, forcing organi
ai-at-work.dwp_take: Veeam is arguing that AI systems proliferating across enterprise infrastructure mean organizations need to rethink backup and recovery strategies for environments they can't fully control or predict. This matters because your disaster recovery playbook from 2023 probably assumed humans were still making the important decisions and your data stayed relatively still. The irony is rich: we spent decades trying to control chaos, and now we're intentionally deploying autonomous agents that create new kinds of it.

digital-culture.title: Technology x humanity: A conversation with Dayforce’s Amy Capellanti-Wolf
digital-culture.excerpt: The HR leader shares her take on the rise of AI, hybrid work and retaining talent.
digital-culture.dwp_take: Dayforce's Amy Capellanti-Wolf is making the case that AI and hybrid work models need to stay centered on actual humans if they're going to work. This matters because too many organizations treat these technologies as silver bullets while ignoring the people side of the equation, which is where everything falls apart. Here's the thing: everyone's talking about technology and humanity like they just discovered fire, but the leaders who've actually figured this out know it's not revolutionary, it's just remembering why you hired people in the first place.

digital-culture.title: Workforce data, smarter AI integration among greatest workplace priorities in the new year
digital-culture.excerpt: The importance of workforce data is just one of the prognostications people managers are making looking to the year ahead.
digital-culture.dwp_take: Companies are finally waking up to the fact that they need solid workforce data to make decent decisions and integrate AI in ways that actually work. This matters because too many digital workplace leaders are still flying blind with half-baked people analytics and AI tools that solve problems nobody asked them to solve. Here's the thing though: having better data and smarter AI means nothing if you're still treating employees like inputs instead of humans, so don't use this as an excuse to surveil people into compliance.

digital-culture.title: ‘Bah, humbug!’ Could employee apathy mean curtains for the traditional holiday party?
digital-culture.excerpt: People say they prefer cash or time off, though some argue office gatherings are still beneficial
digital-culture.dwp_take: Employees are increasingly skipping or expressing indifference toward traditional holiday parties, with many preferring cash bonuses or extra time off instead. This matters because it signals a fundamental shift in what actually motivates your workforce, and continuing to throw mandatory gatherings nobody wants is just burning budget that could go toward things people genuinely value. Honestly, if you're still forcing people into uncomfortable small talk and stale cookies in 2024, you're not out of touch with trends, you're just out of touch with your own employees.

digital-culture.title: As employer burnout costs soar, EY gets at the heart of worker well-being with Vitality Index
digital-culture.excerpt: The tool is designed to help employers measure and boost workforce well-being.
digital-culture.dwp_take: EY launched a "Vitality Index" tool to help employers measure and track workforce well-being as burnout costs keep climbing. This matters because digital workplace teams are increasingly expected to support employee health outcomes, not just deliver email and collaboration tools, and burnout directly impacts adoption and productivity of those very platforms. Here's the thing though: you can index well-being all day long, but if the actual work is unsustainable and people are drowning in meetings, no dashboard is going to fix that.

industry-news.title: Why Factories Are The New Proving Ground For AI
industry-news.excerpt: Except “probably right” doesn’t work in industrial environments; it needs to be absolutely right.
industry-news.dwp_take: Factories are becoming the testbed for AI systems because manufacturing environments demand near-perfect accuracy where mistakes have real consequences, unlike consumer apps that can tolerate occasional failures. Digital workplace pros should pay attention because whatever AI reliability standards factories establish will eventually become table stakes for enterprise software, meaning your organization's tolerance for AI errors is about to get a lot lower. The irony is rich: we've spent years letting chatbots hallucinate in the office while factories have been quietly building the kind of trustworthy AI that actually matters.

industry-news.title: From Insight To Impact: Why Trust Defines Leadership In The Agentic AI Era
industry-news.excerpt: That combination—data, context and motion—is what transforms software from a passive tool into an AI engine for impact.​
industry-news.dwp_take: Microsoft and other vendors are positioning agentic AI as the next big thing, claiming it transforms passive tools into active "engines for impact" by combining data, context, and motion. This matters because digital workplace leaders need to understand what agentic AI actually does versus what vendors want you to believe it does, especially when budget decisions loom. Here's the honest take: trust in leadership matters everywhere, but slapping "agentic" on your AI won't fix broken data or unclear workflows, so focus on fundamentals first and let the fancy terminology sort itself out later.

industry-news.title: iOS 26.5: How To Make The Most Of Apple’s New iPhone Messaging Upgrade
industry-news.excerpt: The latest iPhone software introduced the biggest upgrade to iMessage in years. Here’s how to get the most out of it.
industry-news.dwp_take: Apple just rolled out a significant update to iMessage that actually changes how people communicate on iPhones. This matters because if your organization relies on iMessage for work communication or BYOD scenarios, you need to understand what's changed and whether it affects your security policies and compliance requirements. Honestly, most enterprises should still be standardizing on proper business messaging tools rather than banking on consumer features, but if your users are going to use iMessage anyway, you might as well know what they're dealing with.

industry-news.title: Your AI Model Just Changed: Why Your Document Processing Pipeline Broke Overnight
industry-news.excerpt: ​One model update. Thousands of broken workflows. Here's what leaders need to know.
industry-news.dwp_take: OpenAI or another major AI provider pushed a model update that broke document processing workflows for companies relying on the old version's specific outputs and behaviors. This matters because it shows that building critical business processes on third-party AI models is like building your house on someone else's foundation, and they can renovate whenever they feel like it. If you're using AI to process documents at scale, you better have a versioning strategy and fallback plan, or you're just one update away from explaining to your CEO why accounts payable ground to a halt.
